note: Declarative verification spec. Dynamic provenance (SHAs, digests, changed files) is resolved by tools/verification/manifest.mjs at run time and is NOT stored here, so this file stays reviewable and does not go stale against the tree.

instruments.target: every module contract across 18 test files
instruments.oracle: mixed: mostly the stated implementation contract (regression); four sites use hand-written expected sets independent of the constant under test (P2J-S37 dots, P2J-TB19 extensions, the advisory rule-name deepEqual, FP-01b path grammar)
sharedDependencies: requires production modules as the subject under test (legitimate)
six test files read production constants; four of those close the hole with hand-written expected values
instruments.positiveControl: most tests pair a rejection case with an accepted-safe case
instruments.negativeControl: uneven — present in some tests, absent in others
instruments.doesNotProve: absence of unknown defects; correctness of the contracts themselves

instruments.target: advisory warnings reach a human for every publication-facing value in shipped config, at any depth
instruments.oracle: production lintPublicEvidenceText as subject; the reader is the rendered report
sharedDependencies: PUBLICATION_FACING_FIELDS shared with its own test (closed by a hardcoded deepEqual)
instruments.positiveControl: restoring the pre-FP-01 hand-listed roots makes the completeness test fail, demonstrated; reverting discovery to flat makes P2K-L01/L02/L03/L05/L07 fail, demonstrated as mutant K2-01
instruments.proves: every warning computed for committed config is rendered with its path, including config modules in subdirectories
instruments.doesNotProve: runtime-input safety (QD-J22); semantic disclosure; that an empty advisory list means the prose is publishable

instruments.target: no input in the corpus that the base revision rejects is accepted by the target
instruments.oracle: the base revision's own verdicts, over a corpus independent of both revisions; attribution comes from each side's own error message
sharedDependencies: none: the corpus owns its committed threat list and imports nothing from project-config (pinned by P2K-D01)
instruments.positiveControl: the two Wave 0 shrink experiments now produce 26496 and 32000 regressions respectively, where the derived corpus produced 0; mutants K3-01..K3-09
instruments.negativeControl: base and target identical produces 0 in every bucket
instruments.proves: that no corpus input the base rejects is accepted by the target, that every hard rule and every advisory rule is exercised by at least one input, and which rule each rejection is attributed to on each side
instruments.doesNotProve: completeness. The corpus is a finite enumerated threat list and cannot reach open-set forms — confusable homoglyphs, spelled-out separators, bracketed dots (QD-J13). A re-attribution count also does not bound how far a rule weakened, only that attribution moved.
instruments.reason: P2K-F01 repaired in Wave 3. The corpus was quarantined because it derived DOT_EQUIVALENTS from the module under test and took the extension source from the head under test, so a commit that shrank either constant shrank the corpus policing it. The corpus now owns its threat list and imports nothing from project-config (pinned structurally by P2K-D01). Re-measured on the two Wave 0 experiments: dropping one dot equivalent went from 0 to 26496 regressions, dropping four extension atoms from 0 to 32000, both exit 1.

instruments.target: whether the test suite actually pins each stated contract
sharedDependencies: the SURVIVED/EQUIVALENT split uses the guard corpus probe, so it cannot adjudicate a mutant in any other file
instruments.positiveControl: anchor-exact-once check; PATCH-MISS and HARNESS ERROR reported as failures, never as kills
instruments.negativeControl: byte-difference check rejects a no-op mutant
instruments.proves: for each committed operator, whether some test reacts
instruments.doesNotProve: operator-set completeness; EQUIVALENT is only as good as the probe's resolution (QD-J21: a probe recording only rule names reported a gutted warning message as equivalent)
instruments.reason: KILLED verdicts are decided by npm test and are strong; the SURVIVED-versus-EQUIVALENT split is decided by the quarantined corpus, so the instrument as a whole is not cited as verification until Wave 3 requalifies the corpus Wave 3: the harness no longer reads a suite run from 'did it throw' alone — a run with no TAP summary, or one whose exit code and fail count disagree, is a HARNESS ERROR rather than 'no test failed' (P2K-F09). The split remains corpus-bound, so every SURVIVED outside project-config/evidence.js is strictly 'SURVIVED or EQUIVALENT, undetermined'.

instruments.target: the project's actual closure state, preset values and protected calculations
instruments.oracle: the running product via its real APIs; expected values are hand-written in its test
sharedDependencies: calls production calculation APIs deliberately — it must not reimplement a formula
instruments.positiveControl: renaming or mis-sourcing readySlotCount fails the test (K1-04)
instruments.negativeControl: forbidden-key scan rejects any Evidence prose or private identifier in the output
instruments.proves: the exact project state for the tree it ran against, in a stable versioned shape
instruments.doesNotProve: anything about a different tree; it is a reporter, not a checker

instruments.positiveControl: documented sabotage test: replacing containsHtmlLikeTag with `return false` makes the copy report 19 bypasses
instruments.proves: how index.html behaves in a real browser for the head actually measured
instruments.doesNotProve: behaviour in another environment or browser; anything about an unmeasured head
instruments.reason: no browser measurement exists for the current target head; source inspection is not browser verification

instruments.target: DOM injection probes against the closure UI; no page errors
instruments.positiveControl: asserts the injected markup is present as text, so a silent no-op is visible
instruments.proves: injected content does not become live DOM for the head measured
instruments.reason: no browser measurement exists for the current target head

instruments.positiveControl: asserts the failure text is actually present, not merely that no success text is
instruments.proves: the fail-closed message appears for the head measured
instruments.reason: no browser measurement exists for the current target head

instruments.positiveControl: reads protected values back from the page rather than from the module
instruments.proves: the protected values as the browser sees them for the head measured

instruments.target: the html-like-tag guard versus real Chromium element creation
instruments.oracle: real Chromium — the expected answer comes from the browser, not from the guard, which makes this the most independent oracle in the repository
sharedDependencies: requires production evidence.js as the SUBJECT; the expected value is the browser's
instruments.positiveControl: documented sabotage test reports 19 bypasses on a neutered guard
instruments.negativeControl: parses in both div and table context, because innerHTML silently drops table-scoped tags
instruments.proves: for the 42 generated forms, whether the guard and the browser disagree
instruments.doesNotProve: forms outside the generated set; anything about an unmeasured head
instruments.reason: no browser measurement exists for the current target head

instruments.target: whether a reader without the implementer's context reaches the same conclusion
instruments.oracle: a separate execution context, with scope fixed in advance by the Human Gate
sharedDependencies: the review scope was delivered in conversation and is not committed (P2K-F05); tools/verification/verifier-package.mjs is the first committed handoff
instruments.positiveControl: reviews have returned FINDINGS on heads the implementer believed clean, repeatedly
instruments.proves: an independent reader's findings on the exact head reviewed
instruments.doesNotProve: that the next reviewer can reconstruct the same scope without the conversation

instruments.target: how deep publication-lint discovery actually reaches
instruments.oracle: a synthetic config module planted one directory down, carrying three publication-facing values, one of which trips a HARD rule
sharedDependencies: imports nothing from the guard; observes the shipped lint and the shipped suite from outside
instruments.positiveControl: with discovery reverted to flat the same script reports 0 of 3 values found and the suite green — the measured 'before' column of D-006
instruments.negativeControl: with no probe planted the inventory is unchanged
instruments.proves: that a config module in a subdirectory is discovered, its unpublishable value reported, and the shipped suite turned red by it
instruments.doesNotProve: anything about values outside project-config, or about open-set heuristics (homoglyphs, spelled-out forms) at any depth

knownLimitations.statement: guard-diff and its corpus are blind to any change that shrinks a production constant the corpus derives from. Measured twice; each made the guard accept a private-document filename while the differential reported REGRESSIONS 0.
the corpus has no positive control: nothing checks it contains the inputs it is meant to contain.
diff-heads records only the first matching rule, so a rule masked by an earlier one is invisible.
browser harnesses import Playwright from an environment-specific absolute path; devDependencies is empty by design.
inputDigest now has a schema slot, but no instrument computes an independent corpus digest yet.
makeEvidence can construct Evidence whose prose carries a demoted form, and the candidate serializer copies it; the lint inspects committed config only. Inert while observations are 0.

publication-lint discovery was non-recursive in BOTH the implementation and its test. Measured: three publication-facing values planted one directory down — one tripping a HARD rule — were reported as zero, and the shipped suite stayed green.
knownLimitations.status: CLOSED in Wave 2 — discovery is recursive (D-006); the test oracles are a hand-written literal, git ls-files, and a tree the test builds, so no walker is shared with the implementation

knownLimitations.statement: the lint's expected-side walker is structurally the same algorithm as the implementation's; what breaks the symmetry is FP-01b's hardcoded literal paths.
colon-labelled yen prices are rejected by windows-absolute-path. Accepted cost of the Phase 2J fail-closed decision.

an instrument that spawns a child reads differently depending on who invoked it: NODE_TEST_CONTEXT leaking into the child makes `node --test` print no summary and exit 0 even when a test fails. Measured in the mutation harness on a mutant it otherwise reports KILLED: clean env gave exit 1 with 5 'not ok' lines, the leaked env gave exit 0 with no TAP at all, which the harness read as 'no test failed' — every operator in such a battery reports SURVIVED behind a normal-looking table.
knownLimitations.status: CLOSED in Wave 3 for the mutation harness and the Wave 2 experiment (env sanitised; no TAP summary or disagreeing signals is a HARNESS ERROR). diff-heads spawns only git, which is unaffected.

knownLimitations.statement: the symlink guard in discoverConfigModules is EQUIVALENT under mutation: removing it produced byte-identical output on a tree with file, directory and cyclic symlinks, because withFileTypes already reports isDirectory() and isFile() as false for a symlink. The classification is a measurement on THIS filesystem and Node version; a filesystem returning DT_UNKNOWN was not tested.
knownLimitations.status: equivalent — kept as defence in depth

knownLimitations.statement: the differential corpus is a finite enumerated threat list. It now exercises every hard and advisory rule and is independent of the subject, but it cannot reach open-set forms: confusable homoglyphs, spelled-out separators, bracketed dots. A REGRESSIONS: 0 is a statement about this corpus, whose digest is printed beside it, and never about the guard in general.
knownLimitations.status: open by construction — not repairable, only stated

evidenceStateExpected.note: Hand-written expectation, NOT read from the tree. A verifier runs `node tools/verification/project-state-probe.mjs` and compares its output against these values. Disagreement is a finding, not a tolerance.
